messages:
sophie: Heads-up 1 0000 - UX decision needed: when autofallback kicks in (latency/capacity/error triggers) do we:
  A) return 200 with a reduced "lite" payload (silent degrade)
  B) return 503/4xx with explicit reason (fail fast)

We need a default for hosted + Dedicated, plus a per-tenant override. This affects SDK contract, dashboards, and SLO math. Thoughts? @kevin @lisa

kevin: strong +1 for silent degrade by default. Many customers choose availability > fidelity. If we do 503 by default, lots of noisy alerts and broken UX.

lisa: disagrees for developer-first stance. Silent changes are the worst for correctness. Tests will pass locally then break in prod. hybrid idea: silent for end-user surface but include a header and a telemetry sample that captures original vs degraded output.

frank: ops perspective: whatever we pick, we must standardize the audit event. Need these fields: trace_id, tenant_id, policy_id, trigger_type, matched_variant, sampled=true/false. Also decide retention and export path (SIEM/webhook).

ops-bot: reminder: existing policy schema v2 supports "note" field but not structured sampling ids. Opening an RFC would help.

kevin: if we do silent+header, sdk maintainers need to document header behaviour. propose header names: `x-rw-fallback: silent|strict` and `x-rw-fallback-sampled: 1`. SDKs can surface as Response.fallback_meta.

lisa: also add an opt-in query param for routes: `?rw_fallback=strict|silent|transparent` so teams can force strict during staging. transparent -> still 200 but body includes `degraded_reason` field so consumers are explicit about it.

frank: telemetry cardinality warning: if we include full response diffs in sampled events, that could leak PII and blow up storage. prefer storing only fingerprints + policy_id + small sketch of diff. full replay should be behind operator-only access and scrubbed.

sophie: good point. propose sampling pipeline: 0.1% global default, tenant can opt to 100% for their account, enterprise defaults to 1% with 90d retention. sampled_event schema: sampling_id, trace_id, policy_id, variant, metric_snapshot, minimal diff_url (signed, 7d).

kevin: console UX ask: show a "Fallback timeline" per-route with counts, example sampled traces, and a one-click "replay request" that replays request against current model set in a sandbox. Should we allow replay for private tenants? need legal signoff.

lisa: replay is huge for debugging. require strict RBAC + scrubbed data. UI should show why fallback happened (trigger + rule) and allow operator to create a ticket from the trace.

frank: alerting strategy: we should not tie pagers to every fallback. instead, create severity buckets: info (sampled only), warn (persistent > threshold for X minutes), critical (SLO breach). Operator inbox gets low-severity items, on-call only gets critical.

sophie: rollout plan suggestion: default behavior = silent degrade with headers + 0.1% sampling. Stage 1: implement header + sampling + audit event schema. Stage 2: add per-route query override + SDK changes. Stage 3: console timeline + replay (RBAC). Stage 4: enterprise retention/exports.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled 2026-07-01T09:00 by @ci.

kevin: UX nit: header should be stable across versions. if we decide `x-redwood-fallback` please avoid `rw_` prefix.

lisa: agree on stable name. `x-redwood-fallback` + `x-redwood-fallback-sampled` works. document in API changelog.

frank: I'll draft the audit schema and the alerting buckets. also will sketch retention defaults and export hooks to SIEM.

sophie: i'll write the RFC and mock the console timeline. assigning owners: frank -> audit + alerts; kevin -> SDK/docs + headers; lisa -> replay security + UX; sophie -> RFC + rollout plan. quick emoji if you're on board.

kevin: :thumbsup:

lisa: :thumbsup:

frank: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: created ticket RW-6248 "RFC: fallback defaults + telemetry" assigned to sophie, kevin, lisa, frank.

sophie: thanks all. will post RFC draft in #eng-platform tomorrow for review.
